t: You're on St James's Place, a street near Green Park first developed around 1694. In 1720 the historian John Strype called it a good street, with well-built houses inhabited by gentry. By 1870 Henry Wheatley thought it one of the oddest built streets in London. Several notable people were born here, among them the Conservative cabinet minister Paul Channon and the Anglo-Irish peer James Stopford, Earl of Courtown. Others died here, including the painter and poet Margaret Bingham, Countess of Lucan, and the Scottish peer Charles Douglas, Marquess of Queensberry.
